 IND vs NZ 3rd T20I Wellington Weather: Check pitch and weather report of Hnry stadium, predicted playing 11
 SECTIONS IND vs NZ 3rd T20I Wellington Weather: Check pitch and weather report of Hnry stadium, predicted playing 11 By Trending Desk , ET Online Last Updated: Oct 27, 2026, 09:18:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Ind vs NZ 3rd T20 Wellington Weather Update: India will take on New Zealand in the third T20I at Hnry Stadium in Wellington on October 27, 2026, looking to secure the five-match series with a third consecutive victory. Check the predicted playing 11 for both teams, pitch report, Wellington weather forecast, toss prediction and key players to watch. New Zealand will aim to bounce back despite concerns over their pace attack, while India will look to maintain their winning momentum and improve their bowling performance.
 Agencies IND vs NZ 3rd T20I Playing 11, Pitch Report, Weather Updates of wellington India will look to seal the five-match T20I series when they face New Zealand in the third match at Hnry Stadium in Wellington on Tuesday, October 27. The visitors have taken a 2-0 lead after winning the first two games by four wickets each and need just one more victory to secure the series. New Zealand, meanwhile, will be under pressure to keep the contest alive. Their batters have produced competitive totals, but the bowling attack has struggled to stop India's chase. The hosts will also have to manage changes to their pace attack, with Matt Henry unavailable for the remaining matches and Lockie Ferguson missing the Wellington fixture.
 Wellington Weather Forecast Today: Will Rain Interrupt IND vs NZ Match?

 Wellington Weather Forecast: 
The latest forecast indicates that Wellington could experience a favourable evening for cricket. While the day carries a high chance of precipitation, the forecast shows a sharp drop in rain chances at night, with clear or mostly clear skies expected around the scheduled match hours. Winds are also forecast to ease gradually.
 The main weather factor to watch is the wind. Wellington is known for breezy conditions, which can affect lofted shots, high catches and the control of fast bowlers. Cooler temperatures could also make conditions challenging for players who spend long periods in the field.
 At the time of writing, the forecast suggests that a major rain interruption during the evening is unlikely, although the final conditions will depend on how the weather develops closer to the start.

 India are expected to retain Sooryavanshi in the playing XI, with Ishan Kishan unavailable for the third match because of an injury. The young batter will hope to make better use of his opportunity after scoring four runs in the previous game. The batting order has several players capable of accelerating the scoring rate. Tilak Varma, Naman Dhir and Nitish Kumar Reddy have already contributed important runs in the series, giving India options if the top order loses early wickets.
Bhuvneshwar Kumar will be another player to watch. The experienced pacer has endured an expensive start to the series and will look to improve his execution, particularly against New Zealand's aggressive top order.
 New Zealand predicted playing 11

 New Zealand are likely to rely on their available pace options after Henry was ruled out of the remaining matches and Ferguson was set to miss the Wellington game. Kyle Jamieson and Adam Milne are among the options for the hosts as they look to strengthen their bowling attack.
Glenn Phillips remains a key figure in the batting lineup after his explosive performance in the series opener. Captain Santner will also be important, both for his left-arm spin and his ability to contribute valuable runs in the middle order.
Note: These are predicted lineups, not confirmed playing XIs. Final teams will be announced at the toss.
 IND vs NZ 3rd T20I Pitch Report at Hnry Stadium, Wellington
The pitch at Hnry Stadium, also known as Sky Stadium, is expected to offer opportunities for both batters and fast bowlers in the third T20I. Early movement and bounce could trouble batters, particularly if New Zealand's seamers find the right line and length.
The ground's conditions may also reward aggressive batting once players settle at the crease. India's deep batting lineup could prove useful on a surface where scoring quickly is important, but the visitors will need to avoid losing wickets in clusters.
The first-innings scoring record at the venue suggests that Wellington may not be as straightforward for batters as the high-scoring matches in Christchurch. One recent preview put the average first-innings T20I score at around 153. Short square boundaries could still help batters find the ropes.
 India vs New Zealand 3rd T20: Will the toss matter?
The toss could influence the match, particularly if dew makes the ball difficult to grip later in the evening. The captain winning the toss may prefer to bowl first, although the final decision will depend on the surface and prevailing conditions.
 Key players to watch in IND vs NZ 3rd T20I
1. Abhishek Sharma: India will look to the left-handed opener for another aggressive start. His ability to score quickly in the powerplay could put New Zealand's bowlers under immediate pressure.
2. Tilak Varma: The batter's unbeaten 51 in the second T20I helped India complete another successful chase. His ability to handle pressure makes him a crucial part of the middle order.
3. Glenn Phillips: New Zealand will need another strong performance from Phillips, who struck an unbeaten 82 in the series opener. His power-hitting could be vital if the hosts are to post a challenging total.
4. Mitchell Santner: The New Zealand captain will have an important role with the ball. His left-arm spin and tactical decisions could determine how effectively the hosts contain India's middle order.
5. Arshdeep Singh: India's left-arm seamer could be particularly important during the powerplay and at the death, when New Zealand will look to maximise their scoring.
